Fintech.brief: India's largest venture category by capital, spanning payments, digital lending, wealthtech, insurtech and B2B finance infrastructure. UPI made payments ubiquitous but thin-margin, so capital has moved toward lending, wealth and embedded finance. Growth funds and fintech specialists back later stages while seed money flows to AI-led credit and compliance tools.
tailwinds: UPI, Account Aggregator and OCEN rails cut onboarding and underwriting costs
Retail investor boom: demat accounts and SIP flows keep hitting records
Large underserved MSME credit gap, estimated at over $300B
GIFT City and RBI sandboxes open room for new products
Credit-on-UPI and RuPay credit cards widen the lending surface
headwinds: Tight RBI rules on digital lending, FLDG and co-lending cap growth models
Zero-MDR UPI keeps pure payments businesses unprofitable
SEBI curbs on F&O and finfluencers hit broking and trading volumes
Rising unsecured-loan delinquencies push up risk weights and funding costs
Licence dependence: NBFC/PA licences are slow and costly to get

AI & Deeptech.brief: The fastest-growing pocket of Indian early-stage funding, spanning applied GenAI, vertical AI agents, robotics, semiconductors, spacetech and drones. Most AI startups build applications on global foundation models, with a smaller set building Indic-language models. Deeptech rounds are smaller but rising, helped by government co-investment.
tailwinds: IndiaAI Mission funds GPU compute and Indic foundation models
Semicon India incentives and new fabs/OSAT plants anchor chip design startups
Space sector opened to private players via IN-SPACe and the 2023 Space Policy
Deep engineering talent and low cost to build global B2B AI products
Defence indigenisation and the drone PLI create domestic demand
headwinds: Thin moats when built on third-party foundation models
GPU compute is scarce and costly next to US peers
Long hardware gestation clashes with typical VC fund timelines
Few domestic enterprise buyers pay for frontier AI at scale
Data protection rules (DPDP Act) and unclear AI regulation add compliance load

SaaS & Enterprise Tech.brief: India is the second-largest SaaS hub after the US, selling mostly to global mid-market and enterprise buyers. AI-native vertical SaaS, cybersecurity, devtools and HR/fin-ops software attract most rounds. Investors favour capital-efficient companies with US revenue and clear paths to $100M ARR.
tailwinds: AI copilots and agents create a new product cycle and pricing upside
Cost advantage in engineering and support versus US competitors
Indian enterprises digitising fast (GST, e-invoicing, DPDP compliance)
Proven playbook from Freshworks, Zoho, Postman and Chargebee
Global capability centres in India seed founders and early customers
headwinds: Slower US software budgets and longer sales cycles
AI commoditises point solutions, compressing seat-based pricing
Low willingness to pay in the domestic SMB market
Thin late-stage capital and IPO comps for SaaS in India
Data-localisation and security reviews slow enterprise deals

D2C & Consumer Brands.brief: Digital-first brands in beauty, personal care, food and beverage, apparel and home sell through their own sites, marketplaces and quick commerce. Funding has shifted from growth-at-all-costs to profitable brands with offline and q-commerce distribution. Consumer-focused funds and strategic corporates are the most active backers.
tailwinds: Quick commerce gives new brands instant reach across metros
Rising per-capita income and premiumisation among younger consumers
Lower CAC through creator and regional-language marketing
Corporate acquirers (HUL, Marico, ITC, Emami) create exit routes
Tier-2/3 demand growing quickly via e-commerce
headwinds: Rising ad costs on Meta and Google squeeze margins
Q-commerce platforms launching private labels and charging high take rates
Hard to differentiate; copycat products appear quickly
Working-capital-heavy offline expansion
Slow rural and mass-market consumption weighs on volumes

E-commerce & Quick Commerce.brief: Marketplaces, quick commerce, social commerce and commerce-enablement platforms. Quick commerce (Blinkit, Zepto, Instamart) is the defining growth story, pulling in large late-stage rounds and reshaping retail. Early-stage money goes to vertical marketplaces and tools that serve sellers.
tailwinds: Q-commerce spreading beyond groceries into electronics, pharma and fashion
ONDC lowers the barrier to digital distribution
India's online shopper base expected to pass 400M+
Wider digital payments and better logistics in tier-2/3
Festive-season demand spikes reward scale players
headwinds: Heavy cash burn on dark stores and discounting
FDI inventory rules limit marketplace models
Regulatory scrutiny from traders' bodies and the CCI over predatory pricing
Rider supply, gig-worker welfare laws and rising labour costs
Intense competition from Amazon, Flipkart and Reliance

Healthtech & Biotech.brief: Covers diagnostics, digital clinics, health insurance tech, medical devices, pharma supply chain, biotech and wellness. Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission rails and an ageing, more chronically ill population support steady deal flow. Medtech and biotech rounds are growing as domestic manufacturing incentives kick in.
tailwinds: ABDM health IDs and data rails enable interoperable digital health
PLI schemes for medical devices and APIs encourage local manufacturing
Rising chronic disease and an ageing population lift demand
Health insurance penetration growing after COVID
Low-cost clinical talent supports global CRO/biotech services
headwinds: Low patient willingness to pay for digital consultations
Slow regulatory approvals (CDSCO) for devices and drugs
Hospital chains dominate care delivery and patient acquisition
Patient-data privacy obligations under the DPDP Act
Long R&D cycles for biotech with limited specialist investors

Edtech.brief: After a sharp post-pandemic correction, Indian edtech is rebuilding around test prep, upskilling, vocational training, study-abroad and offline-hybrid models. Investors now prefer profitable unit economics, outcome-linked models and AI tutors over large B2C brands.
tailwinds: NEP 2020 encourages digital and vocational learning
Large youth population needing employable skills
AI tutors cut content and teaching costs sharply
Study-abroad and global upskilling demand stays strong
Hybrid offline centres improve trust and retention
headwinds: Trust deficit after the high-profile Byju's collapse
Consumer protection scrutiny of aggressive sales tactics
Free content from YouTube and AI tools
Coaching-centre rules and regional regulation
Seasonal, cyclical demand tied to exam calendars

Climate & Cleantech.brief: Spans EVs and charging, battery and energy storage, solar and renewables, carbon management, recycling and green hydrogen. India's 500 GW non-fossil target and national EV push create policy-backed demand. Climate-focused funds, DFIs and strategics provide a growing share of capital.
tailwinds: 500 GW renewable target by 2030 and National Green Hydrogen Mission
PLI for advanced chemistry cell batteries and PM E-DRIVE EV subsidies
Corporate net-zero and BRSR disclosure needs drive B2B demand
Falling solar and battery costs improve unit economics
Domestic carbon credit trading scheme being set up
headwinds: Capital-intensive models need debt and blended finance
Reliance on imported cells and critical minerals (China)
Policy and subsidy changes create demand uncertainty
Discom finances and grid integration limit offtake
Long payback periods versus typical VC timelines

Mobility & Automotive.brief: Includes EV OEMs (two- and three-wheelers), ride-hailing, fleet electrification, auto-tech and vehicle aftermarket platforms. India is the world's largest two-wheeler market, which makes EV two-wheelers and commercial fleets the main investment theme.
tailwinds: Rising EV adoption in two/three-wheelers with improving TCO
PLI for auto and components, and FAME/PM E-DRIVE support
Growing urban ride demand and fleet electrification by aggregators
Strong auto-component export base
Vehicle financing and used-car digitisation
headwinds: Subsidy cuts hurt demand and OEM margins
Battery safety incidents and quality concerns
Charging infrastructure gaps outside metros
Competition from incumbent OEMs moving into EVs
Gig-worker and aggregator regulations in states

Logistics & Supply Chain.brief: Covers express and e-commerce delivery, freight marketplaces, warehousing, cold chain and supply-chain software. The National Logistics Policy aims to cut logistics costs from about 13-14% of GDP toward global levels, creating room for tech-led players.
tailwinds: National Logistics Policy, PM Gati Shakti and dedicated freight corridors
E-commerce and q-commerce volume growth
GST simplified interstate movement and warehouse consolidation
Export growth and China+1 manufacturing shifts
Digitisation of fragmented trucking (FASTag, e-way bills)
headwinds: Low margins and price wars in express delivery
Fragmented, informal trucking supply
Asset-heavy warehousing needs patient capital
Fuel price volatility
Customer concentration among a few large e-commerce shippers

Agritech & Foodtech.brief: Includes farm-input and output marketplaces, agri-fintech, precision farming, dairy and fisheries tech, food processing and restaurant tech. Agriculture employs about 45% of India's workforce, but capital has become selective after early B2B marketplaces struggled.
tailwinds: Digital Agriculture Mission, AgriStack and farmer ID rails
Government push for FPOs and agri-infrastructure funds
Rising demand for traceable, quality produce and exports
Drone and precision-agri subsidies
Food processing PLI and growth in packaged food
headwinds: Low farmer incomes limit willingness to pay
Monsoon and climate shocks
Thin margins and working-capital needs in agri trading
Political sensitivity of farm reforms and price controls
Fragmented supply makes quality consistency hard

Media, Gaming & Content.brief: Spans gaming, creator economy, OTT and audio, social and community apps, and regional-language content. After the 2025 ban on real-money gaming, capital moved to casual, skill-free and mid-core games, creator tools and micro-drama formats.
tailwinds: Cheap data and 800M+ internet users, mostly consuming regional-language content
Government AVGC-XR push and WAVES initiatives
Creator economy monetisation tools maturing
Growing Indian game development talent and global publishing
Short video and micro-drama formats driving engagement
headwinds: Online gaming law bans real-money gaming and its revenue base
Low ARPU and ad-dependent monetisation
Dominance of global platforms (YouTube, Instagram)
Content regulation and IT Rules compliance
High user-acquisition costs relative to lifetime value

Real Estate & Proptech.brief: Includes brokerage and rental platforms, co-living and co-working, construction tech, home interiors and fractional ownership. REIT and SM-REIT frameworks and a strong office leasing market support new models.
tailwinds: SEBI SM-REIT framework enables fractional ownership
Record office leasing from GCCs supports flex workspace
RERA improves transparency and buyer trust
Urbanisation and housing demand in tier-2 cities
Construction-tech adoption in large infra programmes
headwinds: Cyclical, interest-rate-sensitive demand
Long sales cycles and offline-heavy transactions
Regulatory complexity in land and approvals
Asset-heavy co-living/co-working needs capital
Brokerage disintermediation is hard in practice

Manufacturing & Industrial.brief: Covers defence and aerospace, electronics manufacturing, specialty chemicals, industrial B2B marketplaces, factory automation and contract manufacturing. Make in India, PLI schemes and China+1 sourcing have made this one of the fastest-rising categories.
tailwinds: PLI schemes across 14 sectors including electronics and drones
China+1 sourcing by global OEMs
Defence indigenisation lists and rising capex
Industrial automation and Industry 4.0 adoption
Strong domestic infrastructure spending
headwinds: High capex and working capital needs
Dependence on imported components and machinery
Long qualification cycles with global customers
Tariff and trade-policy volatility
Skilled shop-floor labour shortages

Travel & Hospitality.brief: Includes online travel, hotel tech, experiential and religious tourism, and travel fintech. Domestic travel is at record highs on new airports, better roads and rising discretionary spend.
tailwinds: Airport expansion under UDAN and new airline capacity
Spiritual and domestic tourism growth
Rising discretionary spend among the middle class
Visa liberalisation boosting outbound travel
Corporate travel recovery
headwinds: Dominance of incumbents like MakeMyTrip
Low margins and high customer acquisition costs
Seasonality and sensitivity to shocks
Airline consolidation reduces pricing flexibility
Fragmented, offline supply of hotels and homestays

HR & Workforce.brief: Covers recruitment platforms, blue-collar hiring, staffing, payroll and benefits, and workforce management. India's large young workforce and the formalisation of jobs support steady demand.
tailwinds: New labour codes formalise employment and benefits
Formalisation of the workforce via EPFO/ESIC growth
GCC hiring boom
Blue-collar and gig workforce digitisation
AI screening reduces hiring costs
headwinds: Hiring is cyclical and slows with IT sector demand
Low pricing power in SMB recruitment
Competition from LinkedIn and Naukri
Gig-worker social security costs under new codes
AI disrupting entry-level white-collar roles

Other.brief: Deals that do not fit a single sector, such as conglomerate platforms, services and niche verticals.
tailwinds: India's broad startup ecosystem keeps producing new categories
Domestic VC dry powder remains high
headwinds: Small category with mixed signals
Hard to compare across business models
